# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b69 — Optional illuminance input per managed cover

This release extends the fully restored, bounded-update **Beta 68** and retains its Home Assistant responsiveness fixes, WAQI scale detection, translations, window pause logic and existing PID/supply/sleep safeguards. The integration's canonical domain remains `environment_manager`, with all existing IDs and settings intact.

## New solar-shading controls, on each cover controller device

Each selected native, same-room managed cover gets three independent Home Assistant configuration entities:

- **Use lux sensor for solar shading** — off by default; explicit opt-in per cover.
- **Solar-shading lux sensor** — choose one registered same-room illuminance sensor, or **Selected room lux sensor mean** (average of currently valid selected room illuminance inputs).
- **Minimum illuminance to close** — configurable in lx, initial **1,000 lx**; range 100–100,000 lx in steps of 100.

All labels are available in the **38 supported languages**, including Greek, German and English. Selectors use real device and entity friendly names plus native IDs for disambiguation. Temporarily offline registered sensors remain in the picker. The per-cover inventory is cached, not re-enumerated on each sensor update, status read or hardware command. Settings can be edited while a physical cover is unavailable, without moving it.

## Safe physical behavior

Lux is an **additional requirement to CLOSE automatically**, never a replacement for verified room temperature, solar elevation, sunny/partly-cloudy weather, selected closed window contacts, cover ownership, announcement requirements or existing cooldown and manual override controls.

When the lux switch is enabled, an automatic CLOSE requires a **fresh, valid, same-room, native `lx`/`lux` reading** at least equal to the selected threshold. A reading of 0 lx is valid but too dim to close. Missing, stale, cross-room, manager-generated or wrong-unit sources hold closing; they are never assumed bright. A selected room mean uses only currently valid explicit room lux sources and does not include neighboring rooms.

The reading, configured sensor and threshold are checked **again after asynchronous announcement and durable intent storage**, so a disappearing light reading or changed setting cannot authorize a previously planned close.

A cover **does not reopen merely because lux drops** when it closes. Its existing conservative reopening logic continues to use the original sun/weather/temperature evidence and only operates covers previously closed and owned by HEM. In particular, the new lux feature does not cut power, change HVAC demand or control lights.

## Validation and compatibility

- Actual-source shade controller tests cover disabled legacy behavior, threshold equality, zero/low/missing/stale lux, foreign-room and synthetic sensors, selected-room averaging, weather/sun/window interlocks, authorization changes and light level changing during announcement or persisted command intent.
- Tests verify that closed, previously owned covers do not reopen because shading reduces lux; existing native-device unique IDs and unrelated cover settings remain unchanged.
- All **Beta61–68** PID, sleep, supply, startup, window, AQI, warning, illuminance and event-load regression tests pass.
- Full Home Assistant **2026.10.4** state-change helper lifecycle checks and real Chromium tests of a 5,000+ entity state inventory remain green. The source patch can be re-applied without adding duplicate handlers.
- These are automated simulated hardware tests, **not** evidence of operation on a live installed motorized shade.

## Install

In HACS, redownload the existing Home Environment Manager repository and select beta **v0.6.0b69**, restart Home Assistant and fully reload the browser tab if its old card resources remain cached. No duplicate integration or manual configuration migration is needed. The manual ZIP installs under `custom_components/environment_manager/`.

To configure a cover, open **Settings → Devices & services → Home Environment Manager → its managed cover device**, set the lux source and threshold, then enable **Use lux sensor for solar shading**. Other covers remain unaffected.
